title: Why Angkor declined
summary: Angkor was already declining in the 13th and 14th centuries before Ayutthaya sacked it in 1431, but the main cause of its decline is unknown.
why: A vast water-managed city fell, a case of how climate and politics interact.
question: What caused the decline of the Khmer capital of Angkor?
evidence: Decline in the 13th–14th centuries; sacked by Ayutthaya about 1431; irrigation works neglected; drought and monsoon shifts documented.
wouldSettle: Dated records showing whether climate stress, war or religious change came first.

theories.name: War with Ayutthaya
theories.idea: Prolonged wars with Ayutthaya and rival factions drained the kingdom.

theories.name: Religious change
theories.idea: The shift to Theravada Buddhism weakened the royal cult.

theories.name: Water system failure
theories.idea: Neglected irrigation and droughts or monsoon shifts undermined rice farming.
